title: Ramified identification of the scalar-extended finite pullback tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation rings and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. There is an integer $e\ge1$, the ramification index, characterized by $\varpi_E\mathcal O_L=\varpi_L^e\mathcal O_L$. For this $e$ the following assertions hold. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ and $B_{F,W,m}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $W=X,Y$, $F=E,L$, $m\ge1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For any cochain complex $P$ of $R_Y$-modules put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$, and
$$D^F_m(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes B_{F,Y,m}),$$
where $g_{F,m}^*=g^{-1}(-)\otimes_{g^{-1}B_{F,Y,m}}B_{F,X,m}$, and restriction and transitions are induced by the completed coefficient projections and quotient reductions [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $T_{a,b}:D^L_b(Q)\to D^L_a(Q)$ for their composite transition, $1\le a\le b$. The canonical reduction maps and tensor associators give isomorphisms of $S_W$-modules
$$B_{E,W,m}\otimes_{R_W}S_W\cong B_{L,W,em},$$
and natural isomorphisms of $S_X$-complexes
$$\widetilde d_m:D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\xrightarrow{\sim}D^L_{em}(Q).$$
The coefficient isomorphism is normalized by $\bar a\otimes s\mapsto j_m(\bar a)\pi^L_{em}(s)$, where $j_m:\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m\to\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{em}$ is induced by inclusion. The pullback isomorphism has local formula
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\longmapsto(g^{-1}(p\otimes j_m(\bar a)))\otimes(j_m(b)\pi^L_{em}(s)).$$
These isomorphisms commute with transitions $m+1\to m$ and $e(m+1)\to em$, and with chain maps of $P$. The same-index map defined by this formula with $j_m$ and $\pi^L_{em}$ replaced by $\iota_m$ and $\pi^L_m$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] is exactly $T_{m,em}\circ\widetilde d_m$. Thus the scalar-extended $E$-pullback tower is identified with the $e$-subsequence of the $L$-pullback tower, and its specified same-index map is the transition from that subsequence, without any injectivity assertion about $T_{m,em}$. All identifications are independent of the unit relating $\varpi_E$ and $\varpi_L^e$.

proof.text: Write $t=\varpi_E$ and $v=\varpi_L$. Uniqueness of the extended absolute value gives $|x|_L=|x|_E$ for $x\in E$, hence $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and $0<|t|_L<1$. Apply the uniformizer factorization in $\mathcal O_L$ to $t\ne0$: $t=u v^e$ with $u\in\mathcal O_L^\times$ and $e\in\mathbf Z$. Since $|u|_L=1$ and $0<|v|_L<1$, the inequality $|t|_L<1$ forces $e\ge1$. Uniqueness of this exponent also gives uniqueness of the ideal exponent: equality $(v^a)=(v^b)$ implies $v^a=w v^b$ for a unit $w$, so $a=b$. Raising $t=u v^e$ to the $m$-th power gives $(t^m)=(v^{em})$ in $\mathcal O_L$. Both valuation rings are Noetherian, since every ideal of the principal ideal domains in the cited DVR statement has one generator.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), coefficient setup; agent argument using the cited local-field valuation and DVR statements

proof.text:
Use the compatible same-index maps $\iota_n$ and projections of the scalar-extension definition to define $c_W:R_W\to S_W$ by $\pi^L_n c_W=(\iota_n)_W\pi^E_n$. Its component at $n=em$ factors through $B_{E,W,m}$: the map $\mathcal O_E/t^{em}\to\mathcal O_L/v^{em}$ kills $t^m$ by Step 1, and its factor is exactly $j_m$. Consequently $\pi^L_{em}c_W=(j_m)_W\pi^E_m$. This proves the coefficient square needed at every level, rather than assuming that the same-index map is already an isomorphism. Put $R^E_W=R_W$ and $R^L_W=S_W$. Write $r^F:g^{-1}R^F_Y\to R^F_X$ for the completed structure maps induced by the finite projections and $c^g_{A_{F,n}}$. At every level $n$, naturality of the constant-ring maps gives
$$(\iota_n)_X c^g_{A_{E,n}}=c^g_{A_{L,n}}g^{-1}(\iota_n)_Y.$$
Indeed their adjoints extend the same map of constant presheaves, sending $a$ to its included residue on $X$, so sheafification gives equality. After projection to $B_{L,X,n}$, both $c_Xr^E$ and $r^Lg^{-1}c_Y$ are therefore
$$(\iota_n)_X c^g_{A_{E,n}}g^{-1}\pi^E_{Y,n}.$$
The limit universal property yields $c_Xr^E=r^Lg^{-1}c_Y$. This proves compatibility on the completed coefficient sheaves by their finite projections.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), inverse-limit coefficient sheaves; agent calculation of their components

proof.text: Apply the canonical quotient clause of the constant-completion equivalence to $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(t)$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and to $A=\mathcal O_L$, $I=(v)$ on the same site. Noetherianity was checked in Step 1; the sites are taken small in the sheaf universe. Thus the actual limit projections induce $R_W/t^mR_W\cong B_{E,W,m}$ and $S_W/v^{em}S_W\cong B_{L,W,em}$. The constants $u,u^{-1}$ define mutually inverse sections of $S_W$, so Step 1 gives equality of ideal sheaves $t^mS_W=v^{em}S_W$. Hence $B_{L,W,em}$ is canonically $S_W/t^mS_W$ with its actual projection from $S_W$. This uses the degree-zero quotient clause only, and imposes no completeness or flatness condition on $P$.

proof.text: For $R=R_W$, $S=S_W$, the map $(R/t^mR)\otimes_R S\to S/t^mS$ sends $\bar r\otimes s$ to $\overline{c_W(r)s}$. Its inverse sends $\bar s$ to $\bar1\otimes s$: changing $s$ by $t^m s'$ changes the image by $\bar1\otimes t^m s'=\overline{t^m}\otimes s'=0$. The two composites are identities, since $\bar1\otimes c_W(r)s=\bar r\otimes s$. These bilinear formulas commute with restriction, and therefore define inverse maps of the sheaf tensor products, including when quotient sections lift only after a cover. Combine with Step 3. By the coefficient square in Step 2 the resulting coefficient isomorphism is precisely $\bar a\otimes s\mapsto j_m(\bar a)\pi^L_{em}(s)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor; explicit quotient inverse using Tag 093M as established in Step 3

proof.text:
For $F=E,L$, let $R^E_W=R_W$, $R^L_W=S_W$. The normalized inverse-image tensor comparison applies to $g^{-1}$, the geometric inverse image defined in the statement, and the ring $R^F_Y$. For any complex $M$ of $R^F_Y$-modules it gives, termwise, a canonical identification
$$D^F_n(M)\cong g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}R^F_Y}B_{F,X,n}.$$
Explicitly it sends $((g^{-1}(x\otimes a))\otimes b)$ to $g^{-1}x\otimes c^g_{A_{F,n}}(g^{-1}a)b$; the inverse sends $g^{-1}x\otimes b$ to $(g^{-1}(x\otimes1))\otimes b$. The displayed maps are inverse by the two tensor-balancing relations. Here $c^g_{A_{F,n}}:g^{-1}B_{F,Y,n}\to B_{F,X,n}$ is the canonical constant-ring structure map of the inverse-image definition; this calculation does not require that map to be invertible. The action of $g^{-1}R^F_Y$ on the last factor is its projected action, so restriction to $R^F_X$ is the one in $D^F_n$. No identification $g^{-1}R^F_Y=R^F_X$ is made.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), before scalar extension; explicit balanced reassociation and canonical finite constant coefficient map

proof.text:
Put $H=g^{-1}R_Y$ and $N=g^{-1}P$. Reassociate the tensor in Step 5, using $(x\otimes b)\otimes s\leftrightarrow x\otimes(b\otimes s)$, and apply Step 4 on $X$. This identifies $D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ with $N\otimes_H B_{L,X,em}$. On the other side apply Step 5 to $Q$ and the inverse-image tensor comparison to $P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$. It identifies $D^L_{em}(Q)$ with
$$(N\otimes_H g^{-1}S_Y)\otimes_{g^{-1}S_Y}B_{L,X,em}\cong N\otimes_H B_{L,X,em},$$
where the last map sends $(x\otimes z)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes\bar z b$, with inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. All displayed reassociations are inverse balanced maps and are linear in the final scalar. Compose the first identification with the inverse of the second to obtain $\widetilde d_m$. On local tensor generators its formula is
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\longmapsto(g^{-1}((p\otimes1)\otimes j_m(\bar a)))\otimes(j_m(b)\pi^L_{em}(s)).$$
Here $p\otimes1\in Q$ explains the implicit $p$ on the statement's right-hand side. The formulas are natural in each module variable; applying them degreewise to $P$ therefore commutes with its differential and gives an isomorphism of $S_X$-complexes.

source.place: Tags 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 03EK (section-tensor-product); agent balanced-map calculation after Steps 4 and 5

proof.text:
Write $q^F_{b,a}$ for quotient reduction from level $b$ to $a$. On quotient representatives,
$$q^L_{e(m+1),em}j_{m+1}(\bar a)=j_m q^E_{m+1,m}(\bar a),\qquad q^L_{e(m+1),em}\pi^L_{e(m+1)}(s)=\pi^L_{em}(s).$$
Both first expressions are the residue of the same element of $\mathcal O_E$ in $\mathcal O_L/v^{em}$; the second equality is the limit-projection identity. Applying these equations to $\bar a,b,s$ in Step 6 shows that its two transition composites both have image $(g^{-1}((p\otimes1)\otimes j_m(q^E_{m+1,m}\bar a)))\otimes(j_m(q^E_{m+1,m}b)\pi^L_{em}(s))$. Thus $\widetilde d_\bullet$ is a map of the specified towers, including their restricted completed-scalar actions. For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, either composite replaces $p$ by $f(p)$ in Step 6 and leaves the coefficient factors unchanged. The pure pairings determine tensor maps, so these generator equalities are equalities of sheaf maps, also on sections that require covers.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); quotient and inverse-limit transition calculations with the towers of def-pur-integral-derived-operations

proof.text:
Since $em\ge m$, let $q=q^L_{em,m}$. Then $qj_m=\iota_m$ and $q\pi^L_{em}=\pi^L_m$, as each equality is reduction of the same ring element. The transition $T_{m,em}$ is induced by $q$ on both finite coefficient factors. Consequently its composite with the formula in Step 6 is
$$(g^{-1}((p\otimes1)\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)),$$
which is exactly the prescribed same-index map. The map $m\mapsto em$ is increasing and unbounded, and Step 7 identifies its adjacent transitions, so $\widetilde d_\bullet$ identifies the scalar-extended $E$ tower with the $e$-subsequence of the $L$ tower. This is a statement about strict towers and their maps; no inverse-limit theorem or injectivity of $T_{m,em}$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); agent calculation of the same-index factorization

proof.text: The maps just constructed use the inclusions of valuation rings, the equality of ideals $(t^m)=(v^{em})$, the actual quotient projections, and the normalized balanced tensor maps. The auxiliary equation $t=u v^e$ was used only to prove this equality of ideals. No multiplication or division by $u$ occurs in $j_m$, the coefficient isomorphism, or $\widetilde d_m$. Thus the identifications are independent of the unit relating the uniformizers. If either uniformizer is replaced by a unit multiple, its powers generate the same ideals, the corresponding quotient rings and projections are canonically identical, and every displayed formula is unchanged under these identifications.
